sections.h2: What kind of city is Brandon, Mississippi?
sections.html:
Brandon is the county seat of Rankin County and a suburb on the east side of Jackson. The city was incorporated on December 19, 1831, and takes its name from Gerard Brandon, an early Governor of Mississippi.

The 2020 census counted 25,138 residents, with a median age of 39.9. Brandon covers about 21.3 square miles, almost all of it land, so there is no coastline or river frontage to complicate a sale. Most of the questions sellers hear here concern age of the house, repairs and the rental rules rather than water.

sections.h2: How did Brandon grow from a courthouse town?
sections.html:
Brandon was small for a long time. In 1900 it had a school, a telephone and telegraph office, a sawmill, two livery stables, two cotton gins, two hotels, six churches and a population of 775.

It is now part of the Jackson metropolitan area, and the Downtown Brandon Historic District sits within the city. The city is run by a mayor and a board of aldermen, with six members from single-member wards and one at large.

City services are local. Wikipedia reports five fire stations plus an administrative central station, and an independent EMS district that the city created in 2015, served by a private provider. None of that changes a sale directly, but it does mean inspections, permits and code complaints all go through Brandon's own offices rather than a distant county agency.

sections.h2: What do Brandon's building permit rules mean if you repair before selling?
sections.html:
Most repairs and alterations in Brandon need a building permit, and the Community Development Department at 1000 Municipal Drive issues them. The city's permit page lists re-roofing, siding, window replacements, decks, sheds, fireplaces, swimming pools and room additions among the work that needs one.

State licensing limits come into play for bigger jobs. Brandon's page says state law requires a residential builder's license for a home in excess of $50,000 and a residential or remodeler's license for a remodel that exceeds $10,000. A property owner can pull a permit personally, but the city warns that doing so makes the owner the general contractor, with personal liability for accidents on the job.

  • New residential permits are often issued within 24 hours of submittal, according to the city's FAQ.
  • A permit generally expires after 90 days if no inspections have been made.
  • A project is treated as abandoned if no work is completed over a year.
  • Contractors must register with the city, post a $5,000 performance bond and pay a $25 annual fee for each registered trade.

The city has adopted the 2018 International Building, Residential, Property Maintenance, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fuel Gas and Fire codes, and the 2017 National Electrical Code. A house with past unpermitted work can slow a financed buyer, so ask the department about permits on file before you list. You can start at the city permits page.

sections.h2: Does Brandon inspect rental houses and enforce property upkeep?
sections.html:
Yes. Brandon's Community Development Department runs rental inspections for single-family dwelling rental properties to check fire safety compliance and general maintenance under city ordinances. The city also lists an Application for Rental Inspection and Permit among its forms, so a landlord selling a rental should confirm the inspection record is current.

Code enforcement covers nuisances on private property. The city names waste accumulation, unsanitary conditions, abandoned vehicles and noxious weeds. An overgrown or junk-filled lot can bring a notice, and a vacant house that sits for months is exactly the kind of property that draws one.

  • Walk the property and clear debris, dead vehicles and tall weeds.
  • Ask for any open complaint or violation notice in writing.
  • Gather past rental inspection results if the house has been leased.
  • Keep receipts for permitted work.

Signs in the historic district need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a sign permit is issued, which matters little for a home sale but is worth knowing if the property is in or near the downtown district.

sections.h2: How do Rankin County property taxes work for a Brandon seller?
sections.html:
Real property taxes in Rankin County are due on February 1 and are paid to the county Tax Collector. The Mississippi Department of Revenue states the same deadline statewide, and says that if February 1 falls on a weekend or legal holiday, payment the following Monday carries no penalty or interest.

The state formula is true value times the assessment ratio times the millage rate. Owner-occupied single-family homes are assessed at 10 percent of true value, and other real property at 15 percent. Because the millage rate is set by the taxing entities where the property sits, two houses of equal value in different parts of the county can carry different bills.

Rankin County publishes a notice for its delinquent tax land sale on the Tax Collector's news page. Owners who are behind should clear the balance before that sale, because a property can be sold at the county's tax auction if real estate taxes are not paid on time. You can use the Rankin County Tax Collector page to confirm office hours and payment methods.

sections.h2: What does a Mississippi seller have to disclose and record?
sections.html:
A seller of covered residential property must deliver a written condition disclosure statement before title transfers. Under Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code, that happens as soon as practicable before transfer in a sale, and the seller should note compliance on the sales contract, the receipt for deposit or an addendum.

If the statement comes after an offer, the buyer has three days after personal delivery or five days after mailing to cancel. If a seller leaves out part of it, the buyer is presumed to be on notice to ask about what was missing.

The deed itself is recorded with the Chancery Clerk. Rankin County is one of the counties that collects the $1.00 archive fee, so the standard recording charge is $26.00 for a deed, including indexing for the first five pages, under the state fee schedule published by the Chancery Clerks' Association. Deeds must meet formatting rules, and any instrument prepared by an attorney must carry the attorney's Mississippi Bar number.

sections.h2: When is a cash sale a reasonable choice in Brandon?
sections.html:
A cash sale is worth weighing when a listing would require repairs, permits or time that the owner does not have. Brandon's inspection and permit system rewards documented work, which is a good reason to list a well-kept house the conventional way and a reason to consider an as-is sale for a house that is not.

Situations where sellers in suburban Rankin County look at cash buyers include:

  • A rental house with deferred maintenance and a rental inspection that is overdue.
  • An inherited house that needs cleanout before it can be shown.
  • A home with unpermitted additions that a lender may question.
  • An owner behind on payments who needs a closing date before a foreclosure sale.

Cash Home Buyers reviews the house as it is. Whatever the buyer, the sale still needs a signed contract, a title search and a recorded deed, so ask each buyer to put the process and timeline in writing.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Rankin County?
faqs.a: Real property taxes are due by February 1. If that date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the Mississippi Department of Revenue says payment on the following Monday carries no penalty or interest. Payments go to the Rankin County Tax Collector.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my roof in Brandon?
faqs.a: Yes, most likely. The City of Brandon lists re-roofing, siding, window replacements, decks and sheds among the work that requires a building permit. Call Community Development at 601-824-4580 to confirm before you start.

Yes. The city provides inspections of single-family dwelling rental properties to confirm fire safety codes are met and the property is maintained under city ordinances. Landlords file an Application for Rental Inspection and Permit.

faqs.q: Can I pull my own building permit in Brandon?
faqs.a: A property owner can, but the city cautions that doing so makes the owner the general contractor and personally liable for accidents on the job. State law also requires a license for larger residential jobs, including remodels over $10,000.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my assessment in Mississippi?
faqs.a: Normally the appeal must be filed by the first Monday in August before the taxes are due. The state tells owners to request a hearing with the county Board of Supervisors and to contact the Chancery Clerk for details.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Rankin County?
faqs.a: The published fee schedule lists $26.00 for a deed, including indexing for the first five pages, in counties that collect the archive fee, and Rankin County is on that list. Each page beyond five adds $1.00.
